responses:
The parent already contains the directed Prim-Steiner seed (Seed B); the regression in Attempt 1 came from deleting Seeds A and C, which were winning basins. The correct refinement is to keep the full multi-seed pipeline and strengthen the *directed* optimization: add a direction-correct relay/splice move to the annealer, using cached reversed-graph Dijkstra paths per destination so a path suffix can be replaced with a genuinely forward-directed v→dst segment. This targets exactly the structural weakness (reroute/splice moves never re-pick segment direction) without removing any working seed.

Reasoning:
- Attempt 1's regression (630.08 → 720.09) was caused by removing Seeds A and C; both are retained here, so the result can only improve on the parent's best basin.
- The strategy's gain mechanism (direction-aware optimization under asymmetric pricing) is implemented as a refinement of the existing Seed B pipeline: the new relay move lets the annealer re-route any path suffix along a genuinely forward-directed cheapest path, which the previous reroute/splice moves could never do (they only permuted whole paths or spliced at shared nodes without regard to direction).
- Compute budget: one extra Dijkstra per dst per seed (≤ ~10 per weight mode), plus O(1) work per annealing iteration using the cache — negligible versus the existing 5000-iteration loops; total runtime stays far below 600 s.
- All paths produced remain valid src→dst node paths in `h`, so validation, `record`, the weight-mode loop, and the Dijkstra fallback are untouched.
